(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | years4 = 2016 | team4 = [[Demir İnşaat Büyükçekmece|Büyükçekmece]] | years5 = 2016–2017 | team5 = [[SIG Basket|SIG Strasbourg]] | years6 = 2017–2018 | team6 = [[Nanterre 92]] | years7 = 2018 | team7 = [[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years8 = 2018–2019 | team8 = [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] | years9 = 2019 | team9 = [[Bàsquet Manresa|Manresa]] | years10 = 2020–2023 | team10 = [[Fukushima Firebonds]] | years11 = 2023 | team11 = [[Gunma Crane Thunders]] | years12 = 2024 | team12 = [[Sendai 89ers]] | years13 = 2024 | team13 = [[Kawasaki Brave Thunders]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2013) * Fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2009) }} '''Erik Murphy''' (born October 26, 1990) is a French-born Finnish-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Kawasaki Brave Thunders]] of the Japanese [[B.League|B1 league]]. Drafted by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2013, he also represents the [[Finland national basketball team|Finnish national team]]. ==High school career== Murphy played [[basketball#High school basketball|high school basketball]] at [[St. Mark's School (Massachusetts)|St. Mark's School]] in [[Southborough, Massachusetts]]. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Murphy was listed as the No. 22 power forward and the No. 79 player in the nation in 2009.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Erik-Murphy-56461;_ylt=Ag07EkBrmxr6qx0WMcBO4XHXO5B4 Erik Murphy Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Murphy accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball]] team from [[2009–10 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2009]] to [[2012–13 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2013]]. Murphy became the 49th Florida Gator to record 1,000 points in his collegiate career and was the only Gator to receive first-team all-conference accolades in 2013. He became a regular in the starting lineup in his junior year and was named to the All-SEC Tournament team in 2012 and 2013.{{cite web|title=33 Erik Murphy|url=http://www.gatorzone.com/basketball/men/bios.php?year=2012&player_id=31|work=Gatorzone.com|access-date=November 12, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113062020/http://www.gatorzone.com/basketball/men/bios.php?year=2012&player_id=31|archive-date=November 13, 2013|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== Murphy was selected with the 49th overall pick by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/bulls/post/_/id/14497/rapid-reaction-bulls-draft-erik-murphy|title=Rapid Reaction: Bulls draft Erik Murphy|date=June 27, 2013|work=ESPN Chicago|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|access-date=August 11, 2013}} On July 10, 2013, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Bulls.{{cite web|title=Bulls Sign Tony Snell and Erik Murphy|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-tony-snell-and-erik-murphy.html|date=July 10, 2013|work=[[NBA]].com|access-date=April 3, 2014}} On November 6, 2013, Murphy made his NBA debut for the Bulls, playing one minute and not recording any stats. He scored a career-high 2 points on three occasions: December 10, 2013 vs. [[Milwaukee Bucks|Milwaukee]], December 28, 2013 vs. [[Dallas Mavericks|Dallas]], and March 13, 2014, vs. [[Houston Rockets|Houston]]. On April 3, 2014, he was waived by the Bulls.{{cite web|title=Bulls Waive Forward Erik Murphy|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-forward-erik-murphy.html|date=April 3, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 3, 2014}} On April 5, 2014, the Utah Jazz claimed him off waivers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-claims-erik-murphy-waivers|title=Jazz Claims Erik Murphy Off Waivers|work=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2014|access-date=August 11, 2014}} On July 22, 2014, Murphy was traded, along with [[John Lucas III]] and [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1988)|Malcolm Thomas]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Carrick Felix]], a 2015 second-round draft pick and cash considerations.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-trade-140722|title=Cavaliers Acquire John Lucas III, Malcolm Thomas and Erik Murphy from Utah|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2014|access-date=August 11, 2014}} On September 25, 2014, he was traded, along with [[John Lucas III]], [[Dwight Powell]], [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1988)|Malcolm Thomas]], and the Cavaliers' 2016 and 2017 second-round picks, to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Keith Bogans]] and two future second-round picks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-announce-roster-moves|title=Boston Celtics Announce Roster Moves|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2014|access-date=October 27, 2014}} On October 27, 2014, he was waived by the Celtics.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-finalize-opening-night-roster|title=Celtics Finalize Opening Night Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 31, 2014}} On November 1, 2014, Murphy was selected by the [[Austin Spurs]] with the third overall pick in the 2014 NBA D-League draft.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/toros_201415_first_draft_pick_2014_11_01.html|title=The Austin Spurs Select Forward Erik Murphy With The 3rd Pick In The 2014-15 NBA D League Draft|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2014|access-date=November 3, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107135057/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/toros_201415_first_draft_pick_2014_11_01.html|archive-date=November 7, 2014}} On July 4, 2015, Murphy signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]] for the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Besiktas adds Erik Murphy|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/167116/besiktas-adds-erik-murphy.html|access-date=July 4, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 4, 2015}} In late December 2015, he left Beşiktaş.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/186362/erik-murphy-reportedly-leaving-besiktas.html Erik Murphy reportedly leaving Besiktas] On January 4, 2016, he signed with [[Demir İnşaat Büyükçekmece]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/186868/erik-murphy-signs-with-buyukcekmece.html Erik Murphy signs with Buyukcekmece] On June 26, 2016, Murphy signed with [[SIG Basket|Strasbourg IG]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] for the 2016–17 season. He will join Finnish national coach [[Henrik Dettman]] who reached an agreement with the Strasbourg IG earlier. On July 28, 2017, Murphy signed with [[Nanterre 92]] for the 2017–18 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/242621/erik-murphy-signs-with-nanterre.html Erik Murphy signs with Nanterre] On February 11, 2018, Murphy signed with [[New Basket Brindisi]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]],{{cite news|title=New Basket Brindisi, Murphy arriva martedì |url=https://www.sportando.com/it/italia/serie-a/264535/new-basket-brindisi-murphy-arriva-martedi.html|access-date=February 11, 2018|work=sportando.com|date=February 11, 2018|language=it|trans-title=New Basket Brindisi, Murphy will arrive Tuesday}} but didn't play for them. On March 17, he signed with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite news|title=Erik Murphy: Acquired by G-League's Blue|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/erik-murphy-acquired-by-g-leagues-blue/|access-date=April 15, 2018|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 17, 2018}} He signed a three-month deal, with an option for the remainder of the season, with the [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] on August 28, 2018.{{cite web |title=Fraport Skyliners sign Eric Murphy and Trae Bell-Haynes |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/germany/bbl/286868/fraport-skyliners-sign-eric-murphy-and-trae-bell-haynes.html |website=Sportando |access-date=August 28, 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=March 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On January 28, 2019, he has signed with [[Bàsquet Manresa|Baxi Manresa]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketeurope.com/livenews-fr/450561/espagne-erik-murphy-francfort-vers-manresa/|title=Erik Murphy vers Manresa|date=January 28, 2019|publisher=Basket Europe|language=fr|access-date=April 10, 2019}} Murphy played three seasons for [[Fukushima Firebonds]] in the [[B.League|B2 league]], second-tier in Japan, before signing with [[Gunma Crane Thunders]] in the Japanese [[B.League|B1 league]] on 25 October 2023, on a one-year deal.[https://www.basket.fi/basket/uutiset/erik-murphy-japanin-paasarjaan/ Erik Murphy Japanin pääsarjaan], basket.fi, 25 October 2023 ==National team career== [[File:EuroBasket 2017 Finland vs Poland 61.jpg|250px|thumb|right|Murphy shooting a three-point field goal during [[EuroBasket 2017]]]] Murphy made his debut for the [[Finland national basketball team|Finnish national team]] in August 2014 in a friendly match against Lithuania. He recorded nine points and five rebounds in his debut appearance.[http://yle.fi/urheilu/rannikko_nostaa_hattua_murphyn_debyytille_-_tassa_ottelun_pistemiehet/7392979 Rannikko nostaa hattua Murphyn debyytille - tässä ottelun pistemiehet] He later played in the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] where Finland's campaign was ended at the group stages; Murphy averaged 6.8 points over five games. He represented Finland again at [[EuroBasket 2015]], helping his team advance from the group stage. ==Personal life== Murphy's father, [[Jay Murphy]], is a former NBA player. His mother, Päivi, from whom he gained a Finnish citizenship by birth, played for the [[Finland women's national basketball team]] from 1988 to 1994. His younger brother [[Alex Murphy (basketball)|Alex Murphy]] also played at [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10157046/alex-murphy-transferring-florida-gators-duke-blue-devils|title=Alex Murphy to transfer to Florida|work=ESPN.com|date=December 18, 2013|access-date=December 18, 2013}} He holds both [[Americans|American]] and [[Finland|Finnish]] passports.[https://www.heinnews.com/basketball/nba/murphy-brothers-will-impact-finland-future/ Murphy brothers will impact Finland future] ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2013}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2013–14 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago]] | 24 || 0 || 2.6 || .231 || .000 || .000 || .3 || .1 || .0 || .2 || .3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| Career | style="text-align:left;"| | 24 || 0 || 2.6 || .231 || .000 || .000 || .3 || .1 || .0 || .2 || .3 {{s-end}} ===EuroCup=== {{Euroleague player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2015–16 Eurocup Basketball|2015–16]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[Beşiktaş J.K.
